ai.heading: MCP connection
ai.access_boundary: Off on first use. Your choice is remembered until you turn it off. When enabled, configured AI clients can read and help edit open documents, including unsaved content; text is sent to the AI service you use.
ai.clear_help: Clear settings and credentials saved locally by Leaf for {{client}} and end its editing tasks. Other AI connections and documents remain.
ai.clear_remote: This does not uninstall plugins in other apps or revoke an OpenAI tunnel or key.
ai.clear_failed: Could not clear settings. Try again. Other connections are unchanged.
ai.saved: Configuration saved. You can enable the connection.
ai.tunnel_help: create or select a dedicated Leaf tunnel and paste its Tunnel ID here.
ai.device_unknown: Not identified. Choose for your operating system and processor.
ai.program_help: Extract the archive, click “Choose connection program”, and select tunnel-client.
ai.mac_title: Mac says it cannot verify the app?
ai.mac_help: Open System Settings → Privacy & Security → Open Anyway. After confirming, return to Leaf and reconnect.
ai.key_help: create a key with Tunnels Read / Use permissions and paste it here.
ai.keep_key: Leave blank to keep the saved key.
ai.add_help: In ChatGPT, choose + → Add custom MCP server. Name it Leaf, choose Tunnel and the same tunnel, and select No authentication. Review the risk notice, then create and install.
ai.starting: Connection program is running. Waiting for local readiness.
ai.help_title: Want AI to help with setup?
ai.help_hint: If your AI can operate this computer and browser, give it the request below. You still confirm login and authorization.
ai.help_prompt:
Follow the official OpenAI guide to connect local Leaf to ChatGPT: create or reuse a tunnel, download the complete tunnel-client for this computer, prepare a connection key, save settings in Leaf, then add a custom MCP plugin using the same tunnel. Prompt me for login or confirmation, keep keys out of chat, and finish with an authorized read-only call without changing documents.
https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/secure-mcp-tunnels
ai.copy_failed: Copy failed. Select the text and copy it manually.
ai.desktop_required: MCP connections require the Leaf desktop app.
ai.error: Connection action failed ({{code}}). Check settings and try again. Your documents are retained.

ai.task_copy: {{client}} is editing. This document is temporarily read-only; you can browse and find.
ai.task_stopping: Ending editing after the current batch
ai.task_ended: Editing ended. Applied changes remain; see the bottom bar for save status
ai.stop_failed: Could not end editing. Try again; the document remains read-only
ai.task_pending_save: Changes are applied to the document but are not saved yet. Check the save notice.
ai.program_help_windows: Extract the archive, click “Choose connection program”, and select tunnel-client.exe.
ai.program_help_unknown: Choose the full archive for your operating system and processor, extract it, and select the connection program.
ai.existing_title: Already have Leaf, or seeing a duplicate name?
ai.existing_help: After changing tunnels, add a new custom connection. For a duplicate name, use “Leaf new connection”; reconnecting an existing plugin does not change its tunnel. Use a separate tunnel for Leaf when running it alongside Ripple.
ai.claude_step1: Click “Add to Claude” to open the extension installer.
ai.claude_step2: Confirm installation of Leaf in Claude. No manual configuration is needed.
ai.claude_step3: Keep Leaf open with MCP enabled, then use Leaf in your conversation.
ai.workbuddy_step2: Leaf backs up the existing configuration and adds its connection. In WorkBuddy, open Experts · Skills · Connectors → Connectors → Custom connectors and enable Leaf. Restart WorkBuddy if it is not listed.
ai.workbuddy_step3: Keep Leaf open with MCP enabled. After enabling Leaf in WorkBuddy, ask directly in the conversation; no selection from the “+” menu is needed.
ai.claude_added: The Claude installer is open. Confirm installation of Leaf.
ai.workbuddy_added: Connection added. Enable Leaf in WorkBuddy.
ai.claude_step1_windows: Click “Export Claude extension” and save Leaf.mcpb somewhere easy to find.
ai.claude_step2_windows: In Claude Desktop, open Settings → Extensions → Advanced settings → Install Extension, select the saved Leaf.mcpb, then install and enable Leaf. You do not need to double-click the file.
ai.claude_save_failed: The extension file was not saved. Choose a writable location with a .mcpb file extension and try again.
